summary: Defines the Free Lossless Audio Codec (FLAC) format and its streamable subset. FLAC reduces the storage needed for digital audio without losing information, with an open specification and open source reference implementation.

eli5.summary: FLAC squeezes sound files smaller like a zip file, and when opened the music is exactly the same as before.

questions: what is the flac streamable subset
subtitle: The open format that shrinks digital audio without throwing any of it away.

tldr.problem: Digital audio takes a lot of storage, and many people want it smaller without losing any information, using a format whose specification is open.
tldr.mechanism: FLAC splits audio into blocks, optionally decorrelates stereo channels, predicts each sample from the few before it, and stores the small prediction errors with Rice codes. Each frame carries its own header and CRCs.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9639 is the Standards Track specification of the format and its streamable subset, with container mappings for Ogg, Matroska and MP4 and a new IANA media type, audio/flac.

today: RFC 9639 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2024. It is not obsoleted or updated by any other RFC.

sections.title: What FLAC Is For
sections.content:
RFC 9639 defines the Free Lossless Audio Codec (FLAC) format and its streamable subset. FLAC files and streams carry pulse-code modulated (PCM) audio with 1 to 8 channels, sample rates from 1 to 1048575 hertz and bit depths from 4 to 32 bits. Most tools are tuned for CD audio: 2 channels, 44.1 kHz and 16 bits.

Compression is lossless, so decoding returns exactly the original data. It works because audio samples tend to be highly correlated with their close neighbors. Unlike general-purpose compressors, FLAC removes redundancy only in the very short term, looking back at 32 samples at most. The RFC says FLAC has low complexity, and both encoding and decoding can be done without floating-point arithmetic.

The format works best on signed samples centered around zero, so unsigned audio must be converted to signed first. It is not suited for compressing audio that is not PCM.
sections.eli5: Imagine writing a long song down in a shorthand that you can always turn back into the exact original. FLAC is that shorthand for sound, and nothing gets lost.

sections.title: The Encoding Pipeline
sections.content:
A FLAC encoder works in four steps, and the decoder runs them in reverse. First, blocking cuts the input into contiguous blocks. The minimum block size is 16 samples (except for the last block) and the maximum is 65535. Too-small blocks waste bytes on headers, and too-large blocks make good prediction hard.

Second, stereo files can use interchannel decorrelation, chosen per block. The options are independent, mid-side, left-side and side-right. In mid-side, the mid channel is the sum of left and right shifted right by 1 bit, and the side channel is left minus right. Non-stereo files MUST be coded independently. The side channel needs one extra bit of bit depth.

Third, prediction models each subblock. There are four methods: verbatim (samples stored directly), constant (one value, for digital silence), a fixed predictor, or a linear predictor with stored coefficients. Fourth, the prediction error, called the residual, is coded with Rice codes using 4-bit or 5-bit parameters.
sections.eli5: It is like guessing the next number in a pattern and only writing down how wrong your guess was. If you guess well, the notes you write are tiny.

sections.title: Stream Layout and Metadata Blocks
sections.content:
A FLAC bitstream starts with the fLaC marker (0x664C6143), then a mandatory streaminfo metadata block, then any other metadata blocks, then the audio frames. Each metadata block begins with a 4-byte header: one bit saying whether it is the last block, 7 bits of type and a 24-bit length. Type 127 is forbidden. FLAC supports 127 kinds of metadata blocks, and 7 are defined.

Streaminfo holds whole-stream facts: block size bounds, frame size bounds, sample rate, channel count, bit depth, total samples and an MD5 checksum of the unencoded audio. A seek table lists seek points of 18 bytes each. A Vorbis comment block holds human-readable tags in UTF-8; its length fields are little-endian, the one place where FLAC departs from big-endian numbers. Cuesheet and picture blocks store CD track structure and attached images, and application blocks are for third parties.

FLAC has no version number but keeps reserved space. Future versions MAY use it without breaking older streams, and older decoders MAY abort on data they do not recognize.
sections.eli5: Before the music starts, the file has a label section, like the sleeve of a record: how long it is, who made it, and the cover picture.

sections.title: The Frame Header
sections.content:
Audio is stored in frames. Each frame is a header, one subframe per channel, zero padding to a byte boundary, and a footer. Every frame starts on a byte boundary with a 15-bit sync code, followed by a blocking strategy bit: 0 for fixed block size, 1 for variable. A decoder that knows the strategy can look for the two bytes 0xFFF8 or 0xFFF9 to find a frame.

The next fields are 4 block size bits, 4 sample rate bits, 4 channels bits and 3 bit depth bits, followed by a reserved bit that MUST be zero. Lookup tables cover common values. The sample rate 0b1111 pattern is forbidden. Rarer values are stored after the coded number. The coded number is a frame number (fixed block size) or the sample number of the first sample (variable block size), written in a UTF-8-like code extended to 36 bits unencoded, or 7 bytes encoded.

An 8-bit CRC with polynomial x^8 + x^2 + x^1 + x^0 ends the header. Each frame header repeats the sample rate, bit depth and channel count, so a decoder can start mid-stream without the streaminfo block. The frame footer holds a 16-bit CRC with polynomial x^16 + x^15 + x^2 + x^0 covering the whole frame.
sections.eli5: Every chunk of music starts with a little label saying how it is packed, plus a check number so the player can tell if the label got scrambled.

sections.title: Subframes and Residual Coding
sections.content:
A subframe header begins with a 0 bit, then 6 bits of type and a flag for wasted bits, the always-zero low bits found in samples padded up to a whole number of bytes. A subframe that has k wasted bits codes its samples without them, and the decoder shifts them back in.

A fixed predictor subframe uses one of five predefined predictors, order 0 through 4. Order 1 predicts the previous sample, and order 2 predicts 2 * a(n-1) - a(n-2). A linear predictor subframe uses up to 32 coefficients plus a right shift, and the shift MUST NOT be negative. Both store as many unencoded warm-up samples as the predictor order, because the first samples have nothing to predict from.

The residual is split into 2^(partition order) partitions, each with its own Rice parameter. Signed residuals are zigzag-folded to unsigned numbers. The high part is written in unary and the low part in binary. A partition can instead use an escape code and store its residual unencoded. All residual values must fit a 32-bit signed integer, excluding the most negative value. If an encoder cannot meet that limit, it MUST write a verbatim subframe.
sections.eli5: For each bit of sound, the file keeps a guess rule and a tiny note about how far off the guess was. Small notes take little room, and a few big misses get special handling.

sections.title: Streamable Subset, Containers and Compatibility
sections.content:
The streamable subset limits what an encoder may use so a decoder can join mid-stream and hardware decoders can size their buffers. Among its limits: frame headers MUST NOT refer to streaminfo for sample rate or bit depth, blocks MUST NOT exceed 16384 samples, audio at or below 48000 Hz MUST NOT use blocks over 4608 samples or a linear predictor order over 12, and the Rice partition order MUST be 8 or less. Appendix C notes that following the subset gives the best decoder compatibility, as do fixed block sizes and, for audio of 16 bits or less, avoiding 5-bit Rice parameters.

FLAC can be embedded in other containers. In Ogg, the first packet starts with the bytes 0x7F 0x46 0x4C 0x41 0x43 and the first page is always 79 bytes. In Matroska, the codec ID is A_FLAC and the signature and metadata go in CodecPrivate. The MP4 mapping is defined in a separate document.

IANA registered the media type audio/flac and created the FLAC Application Metadata Block IDs registry, allocated First Come First Served. Appendix B records past format changes, including the blocking strategy bit and 5-bit Rice parameters, both from July 2007.
sections.eli5: FLAC has a simple recipe that almost every player can follow. You can also pack a FLAC song inside bigger boxes, like a movie file, as long as you label it right.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC calls it extremely important for decoders to resist malformed input. Bad payloads MUST NOT make a decoder overrun memory or use excessive resources, and malformed audio MUST NOT make an encoder misbehave. Output can dwarf input: a 49-byte frame with eight constant subframes of block size 65535 at 32-bit PCM codes for more than 2 megabytes of uncompressed data.

Decoders MUST check length and count fields against their enclosing block before allocating memory. Picture blocks can hold a URI, and applications MUST obtain explicit user approval before fetching remote resources or local ones outside the FLAC file's directory. Seeking relies on coded numbers and seek points that may be invalid, so parsers MUST sanity-check them to avoid infinite loops. Applications MUST NOT execute code found in FLAC files, and the RFC advises fuzz testing of decoders.
sections.eli5: A player should not trust a file blindly, just like you should not trust a note from a stranger. It checks that everything makes sense before acting on it.

viz.caption: FIRST FOUR BYTES OF A FRAME HEADER (RFC 9639)

fields.name: Blocking strategy
fields.desc: 0 for fixed block size, 1 for variable block size.

fields.name: Block size bits
fields.desc: Block size lookup, or a marker for an uncommon size stored later.

fields.name: Sample rate bits
fields.desc: Sample rate lookup, or a marker for an uncommon rate stored later.

fields.name: Channels bits
fields.desc: Channel count and any stereo decorrelation used.

items.label: Streaminfo
items.desc: Whole-stream information. Mandatory and always first.

items.label: Padding
items.desc: Reserved space so metadata can be edited without rewriting the file.

items.label: Application
items.desc: Third-party data with a registered 32-bit application ID.

items.label: Cuesheet
items.desc: Track and index point structure, such as for a CD.

items.label: Picture
items.desc: An image, or a URI pointing to one.

items.label: Forbidden
items.desc: Forbidden to avoid confusion with a frame sync code.

items.label: Constant
items.desc: A single sample value is stored.
